cases.purpose: write with a user-name recipient resolves the user through the utmp login records and delivers the banner, the text and EOF to that user's terminal (independent-model oracle).

files.mkutmp.py:
import struct, sys, time
line, user = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
# glibc/Linux struct utmp (384 bytes): type, pid, line[32], id[4], user[32], host[256], exit, session, tv(sec,usec), addr[4], unused[20]
rec = struct.pack('<hxxi32s4s32s256shhiii4i20s', 7, 4242, line.encode(), b'p1', user.encode(), b'', 0, 0, 0, int(time.time()), 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, b'')
assert len(rec) == 384, len(rec)
sys.stdout.buffer.write(rec)

cases.oracle: Independent model of write(1) (man page and the util-linux behaviour it documents): Debian 13 ships no write command, so no reference executable exists. The model: with a one-record Linux utmp file (glibc struct utmp, USER_PROCESS) naming user u1 on the fixture PTY's line installed as /var/run/utmp by a root fixture, 'write u1' selects u1's terminal from that record, prints 'Message from USER@HOST on TTY at HH:MM ...' to it, copies stdin, prints EOF at end of input and exits 0.
cases.comparison: Contract on the candidate: exit status 0 and the banner, message text and EOF reaching the recipient terminal, observed on the PTY byte stream.
cases.script:
t=$(/usr/bin/tty)
/usr/bin/python3 mkutmp.py "${t#/dev/}" u1 > /var/run/utmp
/usr/bin/chmod 664 /var/run/utmp
/usr/bin/chmod 620 "$t"
printf 'user-routed message\n' | write u1; echo "rc=$?" > rc
printf 'W-DONE\n'
